correctness.rationale: Under strictly positive fitnesses the symmetric/antisymmetric change of coordinates yields exact 2- and 3-phase characteristic polynomials. The endpoint sign partition and quadratic root ordering establish a uniform bound for every d in [0,1]; the 1-phase inequality follows from a column-stochastic norm. A four-phase rational witness makes the characteristic polynomial strictly negative at the largest endpoint eigenvalue, so continuity implies an interior global maximum. All boundaries, normalizations and quantifiers were reconstructed; exact arithmetic checker independently reproduces finite parameter identities and the witness, without being substituted for the full proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected original ecological population-dispersal papers establish stationary monotonicity, approximate growth near full mixing, and evolutionary statements in period-two systems; they do not imply the new uniform 3-phase endpoint bound with sharp positive-integer 4-phase counterexample. Compared objectives, hypotheses and implications rather than titles. Broader differently indexed positive-matrix results remain a residual uncertainty.
residual_risks: Uninspected historical analytical treatments of periodically varying two-patch dispersal could conceal a mathematically equivalent 3-phase endpoint bound.

value.rationale: Distinguishing best extreme migration from genuinely interior optimal migration is a substantive resource-allocation question in seasonal metapopulations. The finding is a complete, natural minimal-period classification for all positive two-patch seasonal profiles: 1–3 phases cannot require an interior choice, while a 4-phase integer profile does. The small numerical growth advantage is not itself the claimed value; sharp structural onset and exact reproducible witness are. No downstream empirical or multi-patch theorem is asserted.
